newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds strongest force in Valepar.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds strongest force in Valepar.

text.p: A bloc of four pension funds has walked away with the largest participation in the Valepar special purpose company (SPE) which administers a controlling stake in privatized Brazilian mining giant CVRD.
Valepar placed the winning bid of $3.15 million for 41.73 percent of CVRD voting stock at the company's privatization auction on the Rio stock exchange May 6.
Valepar members agreed to carve up their cake so that the pension funds -- Previ, Petros, Funcef, Funcesp -- have a total of 39 percent.
That is more than the 25 percent stake awarded to Brazilian steelmaker CSN which led Valepar throughout the privatization process, a CSN spokesman said.
"This does not mean that any one member or a group of members will be controlling Valepar," he said. "Valepar is based on a principle of power sharing."

Valepar's Opportunity Asset Management got 17 percent, NationsBank Corp has nine percent, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank, BNDESpar, also has nine percent and CVRD employees have one percent, the spokesman said.
